targets.authors: Cohn, A., Fehr, E., & Maréchal, M. A.
targets.title: Business culture and dishonesty in the banking industry.
targets.evidence_quote: In our first study, we employed Cohn et al’s4 design (n=128 with a follow-up study of n=80) on a significantly larger sample of 620 commercial (not investment) bankers at a large bank in the Asia Pacific (AP).
targets.outcome_quote: In summary, we do not find any treatment effect among the bankers in the Middle East and Asia Pacific, in contrast to the original main study4, although the results trend in the same direction. Consistent with the original study4, we find no effects on honesty from having non-banking professionals think about their jobs.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Authors explicitly contrast failed banker priming effects with the original and confirm the original null effect for non-bankers. The manuscript does not state an overall replication verdict covering both comparisons. Pooled analyses including original observations do not change the outcome of the new samples.

reasoning: LSE repository cover identifies assigned Nature article and authors; accepted manuscript retains the earlier title Banking culture revisited. New samples test Cohn et al.; exploratory original-data comparisons do not constitute a separate central reproduction target.
